title: Monotonicity conjecture for implied Poisson parameters
statement:
Fix a graph $G$ with vertices $a$ and $b$, and let $ab^{\mathbin{\square} k}$ denote the event that there are $k$ disjoint open paths between $a$ and $b$. For each $k$, define $\lambda_k$ to be the unique number satisfying

$$
\mathbf{P}(ab^{\mathbin{\square} k})=\sum_{i=k}^{\infty}\frac{\lambda_k^i}{i!e^{\lambda_k}}.
$$

**The implied-Poisson-parameter conjecture.** The sequence $\{\lambda_k\}$ is decreasing.
This is proposed as a strengthening of the paper's earlier conjecture on the probabilities of disjoint connections; the source gives no proof or disproof.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08457

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).
source_name: Nikita Gladkov, “Percolation Inequalities and Decision Trees”, arXiv:2408.08457 (2024).
